{"figures":[{"fact_key":"Start date","value":"2023-09-01"},{"fact_key":"End date","value":"2026-09-09"},{"fact_key":"Starting capital","value":1000},{"fact_key":"Total money contributed","value":1000},{"fact_key":"Ending portfolio value","value":4963},{"fact_key":"Total return on starting capital","value":396.3},{"fact_key":"Benchmark return","value":69},{"fact_key":"Return difference versus benchmark","value":327.3},{"fact_key":"Purchases and sales","value":1},{"fact_key":"Worst drop began","value":"2025-02-18"},{"fact_key":"Worst drop ended","value":"2025-08-01"},{"fact_key":"Portfolio value before the worst drop","value":1747},{"fact_key":"Portfolio value at the bottom of the worst drop","value":963},{"fact_key":"Dollar decline during the worst drop","value":784},{"fact_key":"Worst drop from a prior high","value":44.9},{"fact_key":"Highest portfolio value reached","value":"2026-06-15"},{"fact_key":"Highest portfolio value","value":6784}],"language":"en","text":"This was a simple buy-and-hold experience: one purchase of DOCN, followed by staying invested through the whole window from September 1, 2023 to September 9, 2026. The $1,000 starting investment ended at $4,963. There were no additional deposits, so the increase came from the investment rather than new money being added.

The path was very uneven. The portfolio reached $1,747 before its biggest setback began on February 18, 2025. It then fell to $963 by August 1, a $784 decline, or 44.9% from the earlier high. In other words, the position temporarily dropped below the original $1,000 starting amount before recovering. That recovery eventually carried the portfolio to its highest recorded value of $6,784 on June 15, 2026, before it finished the test below that high at $4,963.

DOCN's business results help explain both sides of the journey. DigitalOcean reported continued revenue growth and strong profitability in its 2024 results, but its 2025 outlook called for growth in the low-to-mid teens. That combination could support the business while still leaving the stock vulnerable to high expectations. The company's [2024 results and 2025 guidance](https://investors.digitalocean.com/news/news-details/2025/DigitalOcean-Announces-Fourth-Quarter-and-Fiscal-Year-2024-Financial-Results/default.aspx) provide the underlying evidence. Around the February decline, broader market weakness also pressured cloud and technology shares, while coverage described investor disappointment with the outlook and earlier results as additional reasons for DOCN's weakness [in this market report](https://markets.financialcontent.com/pennwell.bioopticsworld/article/stockstory-2025-2-24-why-digitalocean-docn-stock-is-falling-today). These sources support the explanation, but they do not establish that any single event caused the entire drawdown.

The later recovery is consistent with improving operating momentum. DigitalOcean reported growth in the first quarter of 2025, and in August it reported further growth while raising its full-year revenue guidance [in its Q1 release](https://investors.digitalocean.com/news/news-details/2025/DigitalOcean-Announces-First-Quarter-2025-Financial-Results/default.aspx) and [Q2 release](https://investors.digitalocean.com/news/news-details/2025/DigitalOcean-Announces-Second-Quarter-2025-Financial-Results/default.aspx). By 2026, the company was also highlighting rapidly growing AI-related customer revenue, which helps explain why investors placed more value on its cloud growth story [in the company's Q2 2026 update](https://investors.digitalocean.com/news/news-details/2026/DigitalOcean-Announces-Second-Quarter-2026-Financial-Results/default.aspx). That is an explanation of the recovery's context, not a claim that these announcements alone determined the portfolio value.

Compared with SPY, the tradeoff was unusually large. DOCN returned 396.3% versus 69.0% for the benchmark, a difference of 327.3 percentage points. The extra return came with a much rougher ride: the test recorded a nearly 45% drop from a prior high, including a period when the portfolio was worth less than the original investment. Staying invested therefore produced a far better historical result than the benchmark in this test, but only by accepting a sharp and prolonged decline along the way."}
